sections.html:
Washington's capital is also the Thurston County seat. It sits at the south end of Puget Sound on Budd Inlet, about 47 miles southwest of Seattle, with Lacey and Tumwater on its borders. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 56,724 residents, 2.4% above the April 2020 base.

Much of downtown is built on reclaimed land. A house near the water or on fill can draw questions about soil and drainage, so collect any past inspection reports before you list. Most sellers deal with the city only when they have open permits, a rental, or a lot that could hold more housing, and the sections below cover those, followed by the state and county steps every sale goes through.

Under half of homes are owner-occupied, so many buyers and neighbors are renters or landlords. Treat the $486,200 median as a rough guide across all owner-occupied homes, not a price for yours.

sections.h2: Rain, moisture and what buyers inspect
sections.html:
The climate is wet, cloudy and mild, and November through January bring the most rain. City streets, creeks and rivers can flood between November and February. Summers are less extreme but can reach the 90s. Buyers walking an Olympia house tend to check the same few things:

  • Roof, gutters and downspouts, since the wet season runs for months.
  • Crawlspace and basement moisture, especially in older homes near the inlet or on fill.
  • Moss, rot and drainage around the foundation.
  • Cooling or ventilation for the warmer summer days.

Fix or document these before a showing and the inspection phase gets shorter. A buyer taking the house as-is still reads your seller disclosure, so answer it accurately.

sections.h2: City rules for ADUs, middle housing and rentals
sections.html:
Olympia allows up to two accessory dwelling units on almost all lots, each up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, attached or detached. Middle housing is allowed in every residential zone: up to four units on a lot when zoning standards are met, and up to six within a half mile of frequent transit routes or when at least two units stay affordable for 50 years. That flexibility can raise what a lot is worth to a builder, so mention it if your lot is large. The city offers six pre-approved ADU plans on its middle housing page.

Rental owners have extra steps. The city may require rental registration and, for short-term vacation rentals, an additional permit, both filed through the online permit portal, as the Department of Revenue's Olympia endorsement page explains. A general city business license costs $30 when reported gross income is above $4,000.

  • Permit Center: City Hall, second floor, 601 4th Avenue E, phone 360.753.8314.
  • Counter hours: Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Fridays.
  • Inspections and permit status run through the online permit portal.

Did an old project skip its final inspection? Phone the Permit Center ahead of listing and find out what the record shows.

Washington puts the excise tax on the seller under RCW 82.45.080, with any local portion added. The state schedule begins at 1.1% and reaches 3% on the top slice. Its first band ends at $525,000 now and at $551,000 for sales beginning January 1, 2027, and the other breakpoints rise too, to $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A sale at the median value stays inside the first band for the state share. Phone the Thurston County Treasurer for the local rate at your address.

Notarizing the deed sets the sale date, recorded that day or not, and interest starts if payment is a month late. Take the affidavit, deed and money to the treasurer in the county where the property is located. The Department of Revenue REET page has the forms.

sections.h2: Thurston County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
The bill is split into two halves, one due April 30 and the other October 31, and a weekend deadline slides to the following Monday. Tax attaches to the parcel rather than the person, and no fresh statement is mailed when ownership changes. Deciding who pays what at closing falls to you, so find out whether the year is fully paid. Have your closing agent prorate the year and pay any unpaid half out of proceeds.

Sellers who are 61 or older, or retired from a disability, may qualify for a tax reduction or a deferral. Those programs run through the Thurston County Assessor at 360-867-2200. A deferral is repaid from the estate, so confirm the payoff with the county before closing.

  • Treasurer's office: 3000 Pacific Avenue SE, Suite 130, Olympia, phone 360-786-5550.
  • Special charges such as stormwater can appear on the same bill and are liens too.
  • A parcel is not sold for unpaid tax until three full years of delinquency have run.

An improved residential property sale comes with a completed disclosure statement, though a buyer can waive it and some transfers are exempt. The clock in RCW 64.06.020 is five business days from mutual acceptance unless you agree to another schedule, and rescission rights run three business days from delivery. If no statement is provided, the buyer may waive the right to rescind before or after the contract.

Complete every line, write NA where a question does not apply, and explain each yes on an attached sheet. The form covers what you actually know, so past roof leaks, drainage problems and permit history in an older house belong on it.

Three routes cover most sales, and the same deed, excise tax and tax proration steps apply to each.

  • List with an agent and accept the time showings, repairs and buyer financing take.
  • Go solo, which makes the disclosure form, the contract and the closing paperwork your job.
  • Accept an as-is cash offer. That trims repairs and financing waits, and the price usually lands under a fully prepared listing.

Written offers make the comparison easy, and each buyer should say what you will owe at closing. Watch deed and affidavit timing so the sale date and tax payment match.

faqs.q: What will excise tax cost on an Olympia sale?
faqs.a: The answer turns on your price and the local rate. State tax starts at 1.1% on the first $525,000 and climbs in bands, with new thresholds from January 1, 2027. The Thurston County Treasurer knows the local rate for your address.

faqs.q: What are the Thurston County tax deadlines?
faqs.a: April 30 and October 31, one half each. Any deadline on a weekend shifts to Monday. Your closing agent can prorate the current year.

faqs.q: Can I build an extra unit on my Olympia lot before selling?
faqs.a: Often yes. Olympia allows up to two ADUs on almost all lots, each up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, and middle housing of up to four units in residential zones when standards are met. Call the Permit Center at 360.753.8314 to check your lot before you start.

faqs.q: In Washington, does the buyer or seller owe excise tax?
faqs.a: The seller, under RCW 82.45.080. If a seller fails to pay, the buyer can end up responsible, and unpaid tax can attach to the property as a lien.

faqs.q: Where does the Olympia excise tax affidavit get filed?
faqs.a: File it with the Thurston County Treasurer along with the deed and your payment. Your closing or escrow officer usually takes care of this at signing.
